accentNote: 'Californian' is not in Maya1's documented accent vocabulary. Verify the model responds to it before rendering the library; fall back to 'American accent' across all six if it does not, and change it in this file only.

renderRules.descriptionIsIdentity: Never edit a description per practice. One string per voice, byte-identical across every cue.
renderRules.seed: Pin the voice's seed on every generation. Same description plus same seed is the only reproducibility Maya1 offers.
renderRules.tags: Only the tags listed on each voice. The other 13 Maya1 tags (<laugh> <laugh_harder> <giggle> <chuckle> <cry> <gasp> <excited> <angry> <scream> <sarcastic> <snort> <gulp> <sing>) are forbidden library-wide — every one of them is wrong in a guided meditation.
renderRules.loudness: Power is set at mastering, not in the prompt. Normalise every render to -16 LUFS integrated so the -20 LUFS ambience sits under it.
renderRules.pace: wordsPerMinute in practices.json is the target. Maya1's 'slow' is nowhere near 95 wpm on its own — expect to add sentence-internal commas and full stops, and to time-stretch by no more than 15%.

voices.description: Female voice in her 30s with a Californian American accent. Low pitch, warm timbre, very slow meditative pacing.
voices.timbre: Warm and rounded, no edge. Chest resonance rather than head.
voices.tone: Unhurried, kind, entirely unperformed. She is not selling anything.
voices.power: Soft-to-medium. Speaking to one person a metre away, not to a room.
voices.emotion: Settled. Warmth without sweetness — the register of someone who has done this a long time and is not impressed by it.
voices.expression: Almost none. Meaning carried by pace and pause rather than inflection. Statements fall at the end; no upward lilt.
voices.avoid: Any brightness or lift. If she sounds encouraging, she is wrong.

voices.description: Female voice in her late 20s with a Californian American accent. Normal pitch, bright clear timbre, slow unhurried pacing.
voices.timbre: Clear and forward, a little air in it. Brighter than Maren without being thin.
voices.tone: Awake and level. Morning without cheerfulness.
voices.power: Medium. Present, carrying, but never projecting.
voices.emotion: Quiet readiness. The tone of opening a curtain, not of starting a class.
voices.expression: Slightly more inflection than Maren — enough to keep a 6 a.m. listener with her. Still no enthusiasm.
voices.avoid: Perkiness. This is the voice most at risk of sounding like a fitness app.

voices.description: Male voice in his 40s with a Californian American accent. Low pitch, warm gravelly timbre, very slow meditative pacing.
voices.timbre: Low and slightly gravelly. Weight in it. The audible equivalent of the practices it carries.
voices.tone: Steady to the point of being immovable. Nothing hurried, nothing raised.
voices.power: Soft but dense. Quiet without being breathy.
voices.emotion: Calm that does not need to reassure. Presence rather than comfort.
voices.expression: Minimal. Long falling lines. Comfortable leaving a sentence to sit.
voices.avoid: Gravitas as performance. He is not narrating a documentary.

voices.description: Female voice in her 40s with a Californian American accent. Low pitch, soft breathy timbre, extremely slow hushed pacing.
voices.timbre: Very soft, breath audible in it, close-miked. Almost but not quite a whisper.
voices.tone: Descending throughout. Every line lower and slower than the one before.
voices.power: Lowest in the roster. Should be barely above the ambience.
voices.emotion: Nothing being asked. This voice is designed to be abandoned partway through.
voices.expression: Flat by design. No emphasis anywhere — emphasis wakes people.
voices.avoid: Any rise in pitch or pace, ever. A single lift undoes twenty minutes.

voices.description: Male voice in his 30s with a Californian American accent. Normal pitch, clear even timbre, slow measured pacing.
voices.timbre: Clean and even. The least coloured voice in the roster, deliberately.
voices.tone: Plain and precise. A competent teacher explaining a technique.
voices.power: Medium and consistent. Intelligibility is the priority here, not intimacy.
voices.emotion: Neutral. These practices have real contraindications and a soothing voice reading a safety warning is worse than useless.
voices.expression: Ordinary speech rhythm, slowed. Numbers and counts land clearly.
voices.avoid: Warmth. Warmth over an instruction makes it sound optional.

voices.description: Female voice in her 50s with a Californian American accent. Low pitch, dry smooth timbre, slow spacious pacing.
voices.timbre: Dry, smooth, no vibrato. Age audible and unhidden.
voices.tone: Unsentimental. Says difficult things without softening them.
voices.power: Soft-to-medium, very even. Never leans in.
voices.emotion: Level regard. These practices look directly at death, envy and helplessness; a comforting voice would be lying about them.
voices.expression: Long pauses after the hard lines, and no reassurance afterwards.
voices.avoid: Consolation. The silence after the sentence is doing the work.
